sentences.text:
Uday Pratap Sharma And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
on 10 January, 2025

Author: Rajiv Gupta
Bench: Rajiv Gupta
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
?Neutral Citation No. - 2025:Ahc:5396-Db
Court No. - 46
Case :- Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. - 342 of 2025
Petitioner :- Uday Pratap Sharma And 2 Others
Respondent :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Petitioner :- Aniruddha Ojha,Lakshman Tripathi

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Rajiv Gupta,J.
Hon'ble Ms. Nand Prabha Shukla,J.
1.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioners, learned Aga for the State and perused the record.

2. Although, the prayer made in this writ petition is to quash the Fir dated 16.12.2024, arising out
of Case Crime No.72 of 2024, under Sections 420, 465, 504, & 506 I.P.C., P.S. Laksa, District
Varanasi, but when the matter has been taken up, learned counsel for the petitioners has submitted
Uday Pratap Sharma And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 10 January, 2025
Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164765195/
1

that all the offences, complained of, are punishable up to seven years and therefore, before effecting
the arrest of the petitioners, specific provisions contained in Section 41(1)(b) and Section 41-A of
CrPC be strictly complied with in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in several judgments.

entities.text: Uday Pratap Sharma And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3.  We have perused the FIR, which prima facie discloses the cognizable offence against the petitioners and therefore, the prayer made to quash the FIR cannot be entertained in view of law laid down by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of State of Telangana Vs. Habib Abdullah Jellani reported in (2017) 2 SCC 779 and Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Others reported in (2021) SCC Online SC 315 and as such, we are of the view that no interference is warranted.

entities.text: State of Telangana Vs. Habib Abdullah Jellani reported in (2017) 2 SCC 779
entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Neeharika Infrastructure Pvt. Ltd. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Others reported in (2021) SCC Online SC 315
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 4. However, considering the fact that all the offences, complained of in the impugned FIR, are punishable with a term up to 7 years, therefore, in case of effecting the arrest of the petitioners in pursuance of the impugned FIR, it is directed that the respondents/ authorities shall ensure that the specific provisions contained in Section 41(1)(b) and Section 41-A of CrPC and the guidelines issued by Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Arnesh Kumar Vs. State of Bihar reported in (2014) 8 SCC 273 as well as the directions issued in judgement and order dated 28.01.2021 of this Court passed in Criminal Misc. Writ Petition No. 17732 of 2020 (Vimal Kumar and 3 Others Vs. State of U.P. and 3 Others) reported in 2021 (2) ACR 1147, be strictly complied with.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 5. With the aforesaid observations, the instant writ petition stands disposed of.
